newsitem.title: GERMANY: German policy group agrees income tax compromise.
newsitem.headline: German policy group agrees income tax compromise.

text.p: The German ruling coalition's tax policy commission has agreed on a compromise income tax model setting a flat 15 percent rate for income up to 20,000 marks followed by a sliding scale, commission sources said on Wednesday.
The sources said the sliding scale -- based on Germany's existing tax structure -- would run from 22 percent up to 39 percent for high earners.
German policy group agrees income tax compromise
Finance Minister Theo Waigel, speaking before the commission's final all-day meeting, told reporters an agreement had been reached, but gave no details.
The tax model is a compromise between Waigel's bid to keep Germany's linear model and calls by coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) for a three-band tax system.

The sources said single earners would start paying the 15 percent tax rate on income above 13,000 marks. No final agreement on the top tax threshold has yet been reached, but earlier proposals have put it at 80,000 marks.

The commission is due late on Wednesday to wrap up proposals for sweeping tax reforms to take effect by 1999. Leaders of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition will review the results on Thursday.
